l1: What Windows version and build is the affected machine? (Get-ComputerInfo | Select OsName,OsVersion,OsBuildNumber,WindowsVersion)
What is the exact symptom — complete loss of connectivity, partial connectivity (some IPs reachable, others not), high latency, packet loss, intermittent drops, or application-specific failures?
Is this affecting one machine, multiple machines on the same subnet, or machines across multiple subnets/sites? (helps identify routing, firewall, or infrastructure issues)
Does 'Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select InterfaceAlias,IPAddress,PrefixLength,DefaultGateway' show correctly assigned addressing?
Can the machine ping its loopback address (Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 127.0.0.1) — tests the TCP/IP stack integrity?
Can the machine ping its own IP address — validates NIC driver and local stack binding?
Can the machine ping the default gateway IP (Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <gateway>) — tests Layer 2 connectivity and local routing?
Can the machine ping a remote IP (e.g., 8.8.8.8) without using DNS — validates routing beyond the local subnet?
When did the issue start — after Windows Update, NIC driver update, network hardware change, IP reconfiguration, or VM migration?
Is this a physical machine, Hyper-V VM, VMware VM, or Azure/cloud instance? (affects NIC offload capabilities, synthetic vs. physical NICs, and MTU considerations)
l2: Are there custom TCP/IP registry parameters applied? (Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters' | Select TcpTimedWaitDelay,MaxUserPort,TCPWindowSize,TcpAckFrequency,KeepAliveTime)
Is Receive Side Scaling (RSS) properly configured? (Get-NetAdapterRss | Select Name,Enabled,NumberOfReceiveQueues,BaseProcessorNumber,MaxProcessors,Profile)
Is Large Send Offload (LSO) enabled and functioning? (Get-NetAdapterLso | Select Name,IPv4Enabled,IPv6Enabled) — LSO issues can cause TCP segmentation corruption
Is Receive Segment Coalescing (RSC) enabled? (Get-NetAdapterRsc | Select Name,IPv4Enabled,IPv6Enabled) — RSC can reduce CPU but may cause issues with certain workloads
Is IPv6 fully enabled, link-local only, or disabled? (Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv6) — dual-stack issues occur when IPv6 is preferred but unreachable
Are Windows Defender Firewall rules blocking traffic? (Get-NetFirewallRule | Where-Object {$_.Enabled -eq $true -and $__.Action -eq 'Block'} | Select DisplayName,Direction,Protocol)
Is Path MTU Discovery (PMTUD) working — are ICMP Type 3 Code 4 messages being filtered? (Test connectivity with different packet sizes: ping -f -l 1472 <dest>)
Are there third-party filter drivers binding to the NIC? (Get-NetAdapterBinding | Where-Object {$_.Enabled -eq $true} | Select Name,ComponentID,DisplayName)
What are the global TCP parameters? (Get-NetTCPSetting | Select SettingName,AutoTuningLevel,InitialCongestionWindowMss,MemoryPressureProtection)
Are there routing table anomalies? (Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object {$_.DestinationPrefix -eq '0.0.0.0/0'} | Select DestinationPrefix,NextHop,RouteMetric,InterfaceAlias)
Is the NIC experiencing hardware errors? (Get-NetAdapterStatistics | Select Name,ReceivedPacketErrors,OutboundPacketErrors,InboundDiscardedPackets,OutboundDiscardedPackets)
Are there IPsec Main Mode or Quick Mode SAs established? (Get-NetIPsecMainModeSA, Get-NetIPsecQuickModeSA) — stale SAs can block traffic

l1: Validate TCP/IP stack integrity: Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 127.0.0.1 -InformationLevel Detailed — share TcpTestSucceeded and PingReplyDetails(RTT)
Progressive connectivity test: Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <ownIP>, <gateway>, 8.8.8.8 — identify which hop fails
Full addressing configuration: Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4,IPv6 | Select InterfaceAlias,IPAddress,PrefixLength,DefaultGateway,AddressState,PreferredLifetime
Routing table analysis: Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv4,IPv6 | Select DestinationPrefix,NextHop,RouteMetric,InterfaceAlias,Protocol,State | Sort-Object RouteMetric
Active TCP connections: Get-NetTCPConnection -State Established,TimeWait | Select LocalAddress,LocalPort,RemoteAddress,RemotePort,State,OwningProcess
Firewall profile status: Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select Name,Enabled,DefaultInboundAction,DefaultOutboundAction,LogFilePath
Path analysis with latency: Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <destination> -TraceRoute — hop-by-hop RTT and path visibility
NIC status and speed: Get-NetAdapter | Where-Object {$_.Status -eq 'Up'} | Select Name,InterfaceDescription,LinkSpeed,Status,DriverVersion,DriverDate
l2: Global TCP parameters: Get-NetTCPSetting | Select SettingName,AutoTuningLevel,InitialCongestionWindowMss,MinRto,MemoryPressureProtection,ScalingHeuristics
NIC offload configuration: Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name '<NIC>' | Where-Object {$_.DisplayName -match 'Offload|RSS|RSC|Interrupt'} | Select DisplayName,DisplayValue,RegistryKeyword

Network trace capture: New-NetEventSession -Name 'TCPIPTrace' -LocalFilePath 'C:\tcpip_trace.etl' -MaxFileSize 512; Add-NetEventPacketCaptureProvider -SessionName 'TCPIPTrace'; Start-NetEventSession -Name 'TCPIPTrace' — reproduce — Stop-NetEventSession -Name 'TCPIPTrace'

Detailed NIC statistics: Get-NetAdapterStatistics -Name '<NIC>' | Select Name,ReceivedUnicastPackets,ReceivedUnicastOctets,OutboundDiscardedPackets,InboundDiscardedPackets,ReceivedPacketErrors,OutboundPacketErrors
Route analysis with interface details: Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select DestinationPrefix,NextHop,RouteMetric,InterfaceAlias,ifIndex,Protocol,State | Format-Table -AutoSize
Windows Filtering Platform state: Export-NetIPsecRule -DisplayName '*' | Out-File 'C:\ipsec_rules.xml'; netsh wfp show state file='C:\wfp_state.xml'
IP address lifecycle: Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4,IPv6 | Select InterfaceAlias,AddressFamily,IPAddress,PrefixLength,AddressState,ValidLifetime,PreferredLifetime,PreferredLifetime

NIC hardware capabilities: Get-NetAdapter | Select Name,InterfaceDescription,LinkSpeed,MtuSize,HardwareInterface,Virtual; Get-NetAdapterHardwareInfo | Select Name,DriverDescription,DriverFileName,DriverVersion,DriverDate,InfName
RSS configuration details: Get-NetAdapterRss -Name '<NIC>' | Select Name,Enabled,NumberOfReceiveQueues,BaseProcessorNumber,MaxProcessors,Profile,IndirectionTable
MTU and PMTUD testing: Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <destination> -InformationLevel Detailed; then ping <destination> -f -l 1472, -l 1400, -l 1300 — binary search to find exact path MTU
ARP cache validation: Get-NetNeighbor -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select IPAddress,LinkLayerAddress,State,InterfaceAlias — identify incomplete or failed ARP entries
IPv6 neighbor discovery: Get-NetNeighbor -AddressFamily IPv6 | Select IPAddress,LinkLayerAddress,State,InterfaceAlias — validate NDP functionality
TCP connection statistics: Get-NetTCPConnection | Group-Object State | Select Name,Count — identify abnormal connection states (TIME_WAIT buildup, etc.)
DNS resolution test: Resolve-DnsName -Name <target> -DnsOnly -Server <dns_server> — validates DNS path separate from TCP/IP
IPsec SA analysis: Get-NetIPsecMainModeSA | Select LocalAddress,RemoteAddress,StartTime,TotalPackets; Get-NetIPsecQuickModeSA | Select LocalAddress,RemoteAddress,StartTime

l1: TCP/IP stack reset: netsh int ip reset C:\ip_reset.log && netsh winsock reset catalog — restart the machine to apply changes — this restores default TCP/IP parameters and Winsock LSP providers

Firewall isolation test: Set-NetFirewallProfile -All -Enabled False — test connectivity — immediately re-enable with Set-NetFirewallProfile -All -Enabled True — identifies if firewall rules are blocking

NIC driver reinstallation: Uninstall via 'pnputil /delete-driver <oem##.inf> /uninstall /force' — install latest driver from OEM vendor website — Windows Update drivers may lack server-specific optimizations

Default gateway unreachability: Verify physical connectivity (Get-NetAdapter -Name '<NIC>' | Select Status,LinkSpeed), check switchport VLAN assignment, verify ARP resolution (Get-NetNeighbor -IPAddress <gateway> -AddressFamily IPv4)

MTU/PMTUD blackhole detection: ping <destination> -f -l 1472 (tests 1500-byte MTU), ping -f -l 1400, ping -f -l 1300 — identify the largest successful packet size — actual MTU = successful size + 28 (IP+ICMP headers)

Multiple default route conflict: Get-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix '0.0.0.0/0' | Select DestinationPrefix,NextHop,RouteMetric,InterfaceAlias — remove lower-priority routes with Remove-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix '0.0.0.0/0' -NextHop <unwanted> -Confirm:$false

IPv6 preference causing issues: Disable IPv6 temporarily via Disable-NetAdapterBinding -Name '<NIC>' -ComponentID ms_tcpip6 — retest — if resolved, IPv6 is preferred but unreachable — fix IPv6 connectivity or adjust prefix policy

DHCP lease issues: Release-Renew: ipconfig /release && ipconfig /renew — or PowerShell: Remove-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 -Confirm:$false; Restart-NetAdapter -Name '<NIC>' — forces new DHCP lease acquisition
l2: TCP AutoTuningLevel adjustment: Set-NetTCPSetting -SettingName InternetCustom -AutoTuningLevel Normal — if set to HighlyRestricted or Disabled, causes poor throughput — retest with iperf3 or file transfer

Large Send Offload (LSO) troubleshooting: Disable-NetAdapterLso -Name '<NIC>' -IPv4 -IPv6 — LSO can cause packet corruption on certain NIC/firmware combinations — monitor Get-NetAdapterStatistics for error reduction

Receive Segment Coalescing (RSC) issues: Disable-NetAdapterRsc -Name '<NIC>' -IPv4 -IPv6 — RSC can cause latency spikes or packet reordering for latency-sensitive applications — particularly relevant for Hyper-V and Azure VMs

MTU/PMTUD blackhole workaround: Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias '<NIC>' -AddressFamily IPv4 -NlMtuBytes 1400 — start conservative (1400) and incrementally increase (1450, 1480) to find optimal value without blackhole

Asymmetric routing correction: Add specific host route: New-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix '<remoteIP>/32' -InterfaceAlias '<NIC>' -NextHop '<correctGateway>' -RouteMetric 1 — forces traffic through correct interface

IPsec SA staleness: Remove-NetIPsecMainModeSA -RemoteAddress <peer> -Force; Remove-NetIPsecQuickModeSA -RemoteAddress <peer> -Force — forces re-negotiation — particularly for VPN or DirectAccess scenarios

Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) blocking: netsh wfp show state file=C:\wfp_state.xml — identify third-party callout drivers (vendor GUIDs) — disable via Disable-NetAdapterBinding -Name '<NIC>' -ComponentID <filterDriverID> — test — re-enable

RSS queue distribution optimization: Set-NetAdapterRss -Name '<NIC>' -NumberOfReceiveQueues (Get-ProcessorCount) -BaseProcessorNumber 0 -Profile NUMAStatic — distributes receive processing across CPU cores for multi-Gbps workloads

TCP Chimney Offload (legacy): Set-NetTCPSetting -SettingName InternetCustom -AutoTuningLevel Normal — TCP Chimney is deprecated; if enabled in registry (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters), set EnableChimney=0 and reboot

ECN (Explicit Congestion Notification) issues: Set-NetTCPSetting -SettingName InternetCustom -EcnCapability Disabled — some networks drop ECN-marked packets — disable if experiencing connectivity loss to specific destinations
TCP timestamp issues: Set-NetTCPSetting -SettingName InternetCustom -Timestamps Disabled — some load balancers or firewalls reject TCP options — can cause handshake failures

TCP initial congestion window: Set-NetTCPSetting -SettingName InternetCustom -InitialCongestionWindowMss 10 — default is 10, reduce to 2-4 for high-latency or lossy networks to prevent congestion collapse

Network trace analysis: pktmon etl2txt C:\tcpip_trace.etl — convert to readable format — analyze for TCP retransmissions (Retransmit flag), duplicate ACKs, zero-window probes, or RST packets — use Message Analyzer or Wireshark for deep analysis
ARP cache poisoning detection: Clear ARP cache: Remove-NetNeighbor -AddressFamily IPv4 -State Permanent,Reachable,Stale -Confirm:$false — monitor Get-NetNeighbor for recurring incomplete entries

IPv6 duplicate address detection (DAD) failure: Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias '<NIC>' -AddressFamily IPv6 -DadTransmits 0 — disables DAD temporarily if causing address assignment delays — use only in controlled environments

Hyper-V virtual switch RSS: For VMs, ensure vSwitch RSS is enabled: Set-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName '<VM>' -Name '<NIC>' -VmqWeight 50 -RssEnabled $true — ensures VM receives RSS benefits from physical NIC

NIC interrupt moderation tuning: Set-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name '<NIC>' -RegistryKeyword '*InterruptModeration' -RegistryValue 0 — disables moderation for lowest latency; enable (value 1-255) for CPU efficiency in high-throughput scenarios

l1: Complete IP configuration: Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4,IPv6 | Select InterfaceAlias,AddressFamily,IPAddress,PrefixLength,DefaultGateway,AddressState,ValidLifetime,PreferredLifetime | Export-Csv C:\ipconfig_detailed.csv -NoTypeInformation

Full routing table: Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv4,IPv6 | Select DestinationPrefix,NextHop,RouteMetric,InterfaceAlias,ifIndex,Protocol,State,RouteMetric | Sort-Object AddressFamily,RouteMetric | Export-Csv C:\routing_table.csv -NoTypeInformation
Active network connections: Get-NetTCPConnection | Select LocalAddress,LocalPort,RemoteAddress,RemotePort,State,OwningProcess,CreationTime | Export-Csv C:\tcp_connections.csv -NoTypeInformation

System event log (Network-related): wevtutil epl System C:\System_Events.evtx; wevtutil epl 'Microsoft-Windows-TCPIP/Operational' C:\TCPIP_Operational.evtx; wevtutil epl 'Microsoft-Windows-Dhcp-Client/Operational' C:\DHCP_Events.evtx
l2: Comprehensive network trace: New-NetEventSession -Name 'TCPIP_FullTrace' -LocalFilePath 'C:\tcpip_full.etl' -MaxFileSize 1024; Add-NetEventPacketCaptureProvider -SessionName 'TCPIP_FullTrace' -CaptureType Both; Start-NetEventSession -Name 'TCPIP_FullTrace' — reproduce issue — Stop-NetEventSession -Name 'TCPIP_FullTrace'

NIC performance statistics: Get-NetAdapterStatistics | Select Name,ReceivedUnicastPackets,ReceivedUnicastOctets,OutboundDiscardedPackets,InboundDiscardedPackets,ReceivedPacketErrors,OutboundPacketErrors | Export-Csv C:\nic_statistics.csv -NoTypeInformation

TCP global parameters: Get-NetTCPSetting | Select SettingName,AutoTuningLevel,InitialCongestionWindowMss,MinRto,MemoryPressureProtection,ScalingHeuristics,EcnCapability,Timestamps | Export-Csv C:\tcp_settings.csv -NoTypeInformation
Windows Filtering Platform state: netsh wfp show state file=C:\wfp_state.xml; netsh wfp show filters file=C:\wfp_filters.xml — captures all active WFP filters and callouts
NIC advanced properties: Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty | Select Name,DisplayName,DisplayValue,RegistryKeyword,RegistryValue | Export-Csv C:\nic_advanced_properties.csv -NoTypeInformation

NIC hardware information: Get-NetAdapterHardwareInfo | Select Name,DriverDescription,DriverFileName,DriverVersion,DriverDate,InfName,DriverProvider | Export-Csv C:\nic_hardware_info.csv -NoTypeInformation

RSS and offload configuration: Get-NetAdapterRss | Export-Csv C:\rss_config.csv -NoTypeInformation; Get-NetAdapterLso | Export-Csv C:\lso_config.csv -NoTypeInformation; Get-NetAdapterRsc | Export-Csv C:\rsc_config.csv -NoTypeInformation
ARP and neighbor cache: Get-NetNeighbor -AddressFamily IPv4,IPv6 | Select IPAddress,LinkLayerAddress,State,InterfaceAlias,ReachabilityTime | Export-Csv C:\neighbor_cache.csv -NoTypeInformation

Firewall rules: Get-NetFirewallRule | Where-Object {$_.Enabled -eq $true} | Select DisplayName,Direction,Action,Protocol,LocalPort,RemotePort,Enabled,Profile | Export-Csv C:\firewall_rules.csv -NoTypeInformation
IPsec configuration: Get-NetIPsecMainModeRule | Export-Csv C:\ipsec_mainmode.csv -NoTypeInformation; Get-NetIPsecQuickModeRule | Export-Csv C:\ipsec_quickmode.csv -NoTypeInformation
TCP/IP registry parameters: Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters' | Out-File C:\tcpip_registry_params.txt
Network adapter binding order: Get-NetAdapterBinding | Where-Object {$_.Enabled -eq $true} | Select Name,ComponentID,DisplayName,Enabled | Export-Csv C:\adapter_bindings.csv -NoTypeInformation
Kernel memory dump configuration: For tcpip.sys bugchecks, set via sysdm.cpl > Advanced > Startup and Recovery > Kernel memory dump — path: %SystemRoot%\MEMORY.DMP

TSS (Troubleshooting Script Suite) collection: .\TSS.ps1 -Scenario NET_General -NetLogOffload -NetLogTCPIP -NetLogRouting — run on affected machine, reproduce issue, stop when prompted — collects comprehensive networking diagnostics

Performance counter collection: typeperf -cf C:\tcpip_counters.txt -si 5 -sc 120 -f CSV -o C:\tcpip_performance.csv — create tcpip_counters.txt with: '\\<server>\Network Interface(*)\Bytes Total/sec','\\<server>\TCPv4\Segments Received/sec','\\<server>\TCPv4\Segments Retransmitted/sec','\\<server>\TCPv4\Connections Established'
DNS client cache: Get-DnsClientCache | Export-Csv C:\dns_cache.csv -NoTypeInformation — captures resolved DNS entries and TTL
